newsitem.title: USA: Conn. Gov. Rowland's popularity rises - poll.
newsitem.headline: Conn. Gov. Rowland's popularity rises - poll.

text.p: Connecticut Gov. John Rowland's job approval rating jumped 11 points since June, according to a Courant/Connecticut Poll published Tuesday in the Hartford Courant.
Rowland, a Republican, was rated favorably by 51 percent of state residents. Eight percent said he has done an excellent job as governor, and 43 percent said he has done a good job.
The telephone poll of 500 randomly selected adults was conducted Aug 6 to 14 by Institute for Social Inquiry at University of Connecticut.
Forty-five percent of those polled rated Rowland unfavorably, with 35 percent saying he has done a fair job, and 10 percent rating his performance as poor.
In a similar poll conducted in mid-June, only 40 percent graded Rowland excellent or good, and 55 called him fair or poor.
Rowland, the state's first Republican governor in 20 years, faces a re-election fight in November 1998.
President Bill Clinton's popularity has held steady in Connecticut since June, the same poll found.
Some 54 percent of the respondents called Clinton either excellent (nine percent) or good (45 percent), while 45 percent rated him as fair (36 percent) or poor (nine percent).
